headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty fell for a sixth straight week as global tensions and crude oil weighed.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Crude oil prices surged above $100 per barrel, raising concerns of a global energy shock.
Geopolitical tensions and US Fed interest rate concerns weighed heavily on market sentiment.
Sensex and Nifty extended their losses for the sixth consecutive week.
Key corporate triggers including Tata Sons developments influenced broader market movements.
whatHappening: Sudeep Shah outlined a Tata stocks strategy and identified 23,050 as key Nifty support.
Goldman Sachs named HFCL and Polycab India among seven major AI enabler companies.
Paytm remained in focus following recent market developments.
Nifty and Sensex closed lower, marking a prolonged six-week losing streak.

summary:
Indian equity benchmarks Sensex and Nifty extended their slide for a sixth consecutive week in the previous trading session.
Surging crude oil prices above $100, persistent global tensions, and US Fed rate uncertainty served as key market triggers.
Indian stock markets are closed today for the weekend and will resume regular trading on Monday, 21 September.
